mainTopic: Leniencies for a כהן's wife, the three-month waiting period, a baby born at seven months, and the status of a doubtful ממזר
overview: The amud opens by settling two reports of רבא's ruling. He said the lenient version in the evening and took it back in the morning, and רב משרשיא sharply protests permitting the woman without חליצה. Next, the גמרא asks whether the חכמים made a special arrangement for a כהן married to a woman pregnant with, or nursing, another man's child. The answer is no: every opinion there requires a גט, so there is no lenient view to rely on. רב אחא and רפרם then argue about a man who betrothed a woman during her three-month waiting period and ran away, and רפרם rules that his running away is enough. Back in the משנה, רבא asks why a baby born seven months after יבום is only a doubt when most women give birth at nine months. רב נחמן explains that most nine-month pregnancies show by the third month, and this one did not, so the majority is weakened. A ברייתא then discusses whether a second child is a doubtful ממזר. אביי and רבא read it in opposite ways, and their argument rests on whether the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר, as רב ruled, or הלל's list of family groups, as שמואל ruled.

steps.title: רבא changed his mind overnight
steps.stepSummary: The two different reports of רבא's ruling are both true: he said one thing in the evening and took it back in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the evening רבא said it this way, and in the morning he took it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא tells the other scholar why they quoted רבא differently. רבא really did say the other version in the evening, but he took it back in the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two students reported conflicting rulings in רבא's name. רב משרשיא does not call the other report a mistake. He says it was רבא's evening ruling, which רבא replaced in the morning with the stricter version that requires חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: In the evening
In the morning
He took back what he said; he retracted

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one of the people quoting רבא made a mistake. Both quotes are correct; the morning version is רבא's final position.

phrases.english: In the evening Rava said it this way,
phrases.notes: "This way" means the version just quoted, the one the other student reported.

phrases.english: and in the morning he retracted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוּרְתָּא אֲמַר רָבָא הָכִי, וּבְצַפְרָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the conflict between two reports of רבא's ruling from the earlier discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both reports are true, said at different times
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One of the two reports of רבא must be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both were said; רבא retracted his evening ruling in the morning.

steps.title: רב משרשיא objects sharply to the leniency
steps.stepSummary: רב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא sarcastically protests permitting her without חליצה, as if one might as well permit forbidden fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are permitting her? May it be God's will that you permit forbidden fat too!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone strongly protests the lenient ruling. He uses sarcasm to show how obviously forbidden he thinks it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing this to חלב (forbidden fat) shows how strongly he feels. To him, the woman's need for חליצה is as clear as the איסור of חלב. It is an emotional rejection of the leniency, not a step-by-step proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Did you permit her?
May it be God's will
Forbidden fat (חֵלֶב)
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום

phrases.english: He said to him: You permitted her?
May it be His will that you permit even forbidden fat!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter in round brackets. Either way, it means "that you permit."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁרִיתוּהָ? יְהֵא רַעֲוָא דְּתִשְׁתְּרוֹ אַף תַּרְבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts against permitting the woman without חליצה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that permits the woman without חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The need for חליצה is as obvious as the איסור of חלב, so permitting her is unthinkable.

steps.title: Is there a special arrangement for a priest who married a pregnant or nursing woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the חכמים made a special fix for a כהן who married a woman pregnant with, or nursing, another man's child.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, in the case of a woman pregnant with another man's child, or nursing another man's child, who married a כהן, what is the law? Did the חכמים make a special arrangement for the כהן, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the leniency given to a כהן's wife, the גמרא asks whether there is a similar leniency in a different case. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman pregnant with or nursing another man's child may not remarry right away. If she does, her new husband must send her away. For a כהן, a גט would forbid her to him forever, because a כהן may not marry a divorcee. So the question is whether the חכמים let him simply separate from her without a גט, just as they were lenient with the כהן's wife in the earlier case.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman pregnant with another man's child
A woman nursing another man's child
A rabbinic enactment, a special fix
A priest, who may not marry a divorcee

steps.whyThisMatters: It tests whether the leniency for a כהן is a general rule or depends on the details of each case.

phrases.english: Here, regarding a woman pregnant by another man
or nursing another man's child, who is married to a priest, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי עֲבוּד רַבָּנַן תַּקַּנְתָּא לְכֹהֵן, אוֹ לָא.
phrases.english: Did the Sages make an enactment for the priest, or not?
phrases.notes: The "enactment" would let him just separate from her, without giving a גט that would forbid her to him forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי עֲבוּד רַבָּנַן תַּקַּנְתָּא לְכֹהֵן, אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the leniency shown to a כהן's wife and asks whether it extends to a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כהן married to a pregnant or nursing woman may separate from her without a גט

steps.title: Why the earlier case allowed leniency
steps.stepSummary: The cases are different. In the case of the baby who died, the רבנן hold the baby was fully viable, so a כהן's wife can rely on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can you compare them? It makes sense there: the רבנן argue with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and say that even if the baby did not live thirty days, it was a full, viable child. So for a כהן's wife, where there is no other way, we follow the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer begins by rejecting the comparison. It explains what made leniency possible in the earlier case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the baby case, there is a real opinion that she needs no חליצה at all: the רבנן say the baby counted as viable. Since חליצה would forbid her to a כהן, we rely on that lenient opinion for her. The leniency works only because some existing opinion supports it.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? These are not the same
It makes sense in that case
A full, viable child
There is no other way

phrases.english: He said to him: How can these be compared?
Granted, there,
phrases.notes: "There" is the earlier case of a baby who died within its first thirty days.

phrases.english: since there are the Rabbis who disagree with
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא שְׁהָא
phrases.english: who say: even though it did not survive thirty days,
it is a full-fledged offspring,

phrases.aramaic: גַּבֵּי אֵשֶׁת כֹּהֵן כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר —
phrases.english: regarding a priest's wife, since there is no other way,
phrases.notes: There's no other way because חליצה would forbid her to her husband, the כהן.

phrases.english: we act in accordance with the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא? בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question by showing what was special about the earlier case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The earlier leniency rested on an existing opinion, that of the רבנן, which needs no חליצה.

steps.title: No opinion lets the priest skip the bill of divorce
steps.stepSummary: For the pregnant or nursing woman, both רבי מאיר and the רבנן require a גט, so there is no lenient opinion to rely on.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, whose opinion would we follow? If רבי מאיר, he says the husband must divorce her and never take her back. If the רבנן, they also say he must divorce her with a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer finishes by showing that in this case every opinion requires a גט. So the חכמים made no special arrangement for the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is strict: divorce, and never remarry. The רבנן are milder: divorce, and he may remarry her later. But both still require a גט. Since no existing opinion lets him skip the גט, there is nothing to rely on for a leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion would we follow?
He must divorce her and never take her back
A bill of divorce

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים were lenient for a כהן only where an existing opinion already supported the leniency. With a pregnant or nursing woman, every opinion requires a גט, so the כהן gets no special arrangement.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן are milder than רבי מאיר here, but even they require a גט. Being "milder" does not mean they let him skip the divorce.

phrases.english: But here, in accordance with whom shall we act?
If like Rabbi Meir, he said:
he must divorce her and never take her back,
and if like the Rabbis, they say it is with a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison begun in the previous step and answers the question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No special arrangement was made for a כהן married to a pregnant or nursing woman. He must give a גט.

steps.title: A man betroths during the three months and runs away
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רפרם argue about a man who betrothed a woman during her three-month waiting period and then fled. One says we put him in שמתא. The other says his running away is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If a man betrothed a woman within the three months and then ran away, רב אחא and רפרם argue about it. One says we put him in שמתא. The other says his running away is enough for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between two אמוראים. The case is a man who betrothed a woman too early, during her waiting period, and then fled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman must wait three months before remarrying, so we can tell whose baby it is if she is pregnant. The חכמים forbade even betrothing her during that time. One opinion punishes the man with שמתא for breaking this rule. The other says his running away shows he will not marry her too soon, so no further punishment is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces an argument between אמוראים)
He betrothed her
We put him in שמתא (a form of excommunication)
His running away is enough for him

phrases.english: It was stated: If he betrothed her within the three and fled,
phrases.notes: "The three" are the three months a divorced woman or widow must wait before remarrying.

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Rafram disagree about it.
One said: We excommunicate him.
And one said: His flight is enough for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the three-month waiting period. It is not a continuation of the כהן discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether a man who betrothed a woman during her three months and fled gets שמתא, or whether his running away is enough.

steps.title: In a real case, רפרם said running away is enough
steps.stepSummary: A real case came up, and רפרם ruled that the man's running away was enough, so he was not put in שמתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a real case, and רפרם told them: His running away is enough for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how the argument played out in an actual case. רפרם ruled the lenient way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we did not know which אמורא held which opinion. This story shows that רפרם is the one who said running away is enough, and that this is how he ruled in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: There was an actual case

steps.whatToRemember: A man who betrothed a woman during her three months and then ran away is not put in שמתא. His running away is enough, as רפרם ruled.

phrases.english: There was an incident,
and Rafram said to them: His flight is enough for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the argument from step 6 with a real-life ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice we follow רפרם: running away is enough, and there is no שמתא.

steps.title: Why not follow the majority of women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about a baby born seven months after יבום. רבא asks רב נחמן why this is called a doubt, since most women give birth after nine months.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "It is a doubt whether he is a nine-month baby," and so on. רבא said to רב נחמן: Let us say, "Follow the majority of women," and most women give birth after nine months!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its words. רבא then challenges the משנה's ruling that the case is only a doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the baby as a doubt: he could be the first husband's baby at nine months, or the יבם's baby at seven months. Because of this doubt, the יבם and יבמה bring an אשם תלוי. רבא argues that we should follow the majority and assume nine months. That would mean the baby is the first husband's, so the יבום was forbidden, and they should bring a definite חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt whether the baby is a nine-month baby
Follow the majority (a basic rule for deciding doubts)
Let us say (a suggestion that pushes against the ruling)

phrases.english: "A doubt whether he is a nine-month baby," etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about a baby born seven months after the יבם married the widow.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Let us say: Follow the majority of women,
and most women give birth at nine months!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: לֵימָא הַלֵּךְ אַחַר רוֹב נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side topic to the משנה's case of the seven-month birth.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the case is only a doubt, which leads to an אשם תלוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of following the majority should settle the doubt: assume nine months, so the baby is the first husband's.

steps.title: Women in our family give birth at seven months
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the women in his family give birth after seven months, so nine months cannot simply be assumed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Our women give birth after seven months.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a first answer to רבא's challenge. He points to the women he knows, who give birth after seven months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן is saying that seven-month births are common, as his own family shows. So it is not obvious that this baby is a nine-month baby. This answer is pushed back on in the very next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Our women (the women of our family)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נְשֵׁי דִּידַן, לְשִׁבְעָה יָלְדָן.
phrases.english: He said to him: Our women give birth at seven months.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נְשֵׁי דִּידַן, לְשִׁבְעָה יָלְדָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Most women give birth at nine months, so assume nine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Seven-month births happen often enough, as the women in רב נחמן's family show.

steps.title: Is your family the majority of the world?
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects that answer: one family does not make up most of the world's women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Are the women of your family the majority of the world?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב נחמן's answer. One family cannot outweigh the general majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of following the majority looks at women in general, not at one family. So the fact that רב נחמן's family gives birth at seven months does not change the general majority of nine-month births.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority of the world

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נְשֵׁי דִּידְכוּ הָווּ רוּבָּא דְּעָלְמָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Are your women the majority of the world?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נְשֵׁי דִּידְכוּ הָווּ רוּבָּא דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that his family's seven-month births weaken the majority.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A small group cannot override the majority of all women.

steps.title: This woman's majority is weakened
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains what he meant. Most women do give birth at nine months, but a nine-month pregnancy shows by the third month. This woman's pregnancy did not show then, so the majority is weakened for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: This is what I mean. Most women give birth at nine months, and a minority at seven. Every woman who gives birth at nine months has a pregnancy that shows by a third of her term. This woman's pregnancy did not show by a third of her term, so the majority is weakened in her case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains his answer more carefully. He agrees with the general majority, but shows why it does not apply well to this particular woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן does not deny that most women give birth at nine months. But a nine-month pregnancy usually shows by the third month. If this baby were the first husband's, she would have looked pregnant by the time of the יבום, and she did not. That fact pushes against the majority, so the case stays a real doubt and the משנה's אשם תלוי makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I mean (clarifying an earlier statement)
Her fetus is visible, meaning the pregnancy shows
A third of her days, meaning about three months into the pregnancy
The majority is weakened, so it cannot be relied on

steps.whatToRemember: A majority can be weakened by a specific sign in the case itself. Here, the pregnancy did not show by the third month, so the case stays a doubt and the יבם and יבמה bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying that most women give birth at seven months. He agrees that most give birth at nine. His point is that this specific woman shows a sign that goes against the majority.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that following the majority is not automatic. A clear sign in the specific case can weaken the majority.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I am saying:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹב נָשִׁים יָלְדָן לְתִשְׁעָה, וּמִיעוּט לְשִׁבְעָה,
phrases.english: Most women give birth at nine months, and a minority at seven,
and every woman who gives birth at nine months,
her fetus is visible after a third of her days.

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ, הוֹאִיל וְלֹא הוּכַּר עוּבָּרָהּ לִשְׁלִישׁ יָמֶיהָ —
phrases.english: And this one, since her fetus was not visible after a third of her days,
the majority is weakened for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-explains רב נחמן's answer in a way that holds up against רבא's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarification of the earlier answer: the majority is weakened by a specific sign
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's family was meant to outweigh the general majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general majority stands, but this woman's pregnancy did not show by the third month, so the majority is weakened and the case stays a doubt.

steps.title: If every nine-month pregnancy shows, the baby is surely the יבם's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's wording. If every nine-month pregnancy shows by the third month, then this one, which did not show, must be a seven-month baby from the יבם, and there is no doubt at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If every woman who gives birth at nine months shows her pregnancy by a third of her term, then this woman, whose pregnancy did not show by then, is surely carrying a seven-month baby from the later husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on how רב נחמן worded his answer. If his rule is true for every woman, there would be no doubt left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the baby as a doubt: maybe from the dead husband, maybe from the יבם. But if 'every' nine-month pregnancy shows by three months, then 'it did not show' proves it is not a nine-month baby. That would make the baby certainly the יבם's, and the doubt in the משנה would disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: A third of her pregnancy, about three months of nine
Was noticed, could be seen
A seven-month baby
The later one, the second husband

phrases.english: If every woman who gives birth at nine months
her pregnancy shows by a third of her term,
then here, since it did not show by a third of her term,
her baby is surely a seven-month baby
from the later husband!
phrases.notes: The 'later husband' is the יבם, who married her after her first husband died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רב נחמן's explanation from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that a nine-month pregnancy shows by the third month
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule holds for every woman, the missing sign proves a seven-month baby from the יבם, which removes the doubt the משנה assumes.

steps.title: Most nine-month pregnancies show, so the majority is only weakened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רב נחמן: most nine-month pregnancies show by three months. Since this one did not show, the 'most women give birth at nine months' rule is weakened for her, and the case stays a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: in most cases, a woman who gives birth at nine months shows her pregnancy by a third of her term. Since this one did not show, the majority rule is weakened for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording to 'most' instead of 'every'. This keeps the case a real doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two majorities pulling against each other. Most women give birth at nine months, which points to the dead husband. But most nine-month pregnancies show by three months, and this one did not, which points to the יבם. Neither side wins, so it stays a doubt, just as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, read it this way
Most, the majority
Was weakened

steps.whatToRemember: The baby's father stays a doubt because two majorities point opposite ways: most births are at nine months, but most nine-month pregnancies show early, and this one did not.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
most women who give birth at nine months —
their pregnancy shows by a third of their term,
and this one, since it did not show by a third of her term —
the majority is weakened for her.
phrases.notes: The 'majority' here is the rule that most women give birth at nine months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by changing 'every' to 'most'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every nine-month pregnancy shows by three months, so this baby is surely the יבם's.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only most do, so the majority is weakened but not reversed, and the case stays a doubt.

steps.title: ברייתא: first child kosher, second child a doubtful ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the first child born after the יבום can even be a כהן גדול. But a second child is a ממזר because of the doubt. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says there is no ממזר from a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the first child is fit to be a כהן גדול, and the second child is a ממזר because of a doubt. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: there is no ממזר from a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the children in our case. It sets up a disagreement whose meaning will be asked about next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first child is kosher no matter whose he is. If he is the dead husband's, then the יבום was not allowed, since a widow with a child has no יבום. She is then forbidden to the יבם as his brother's wife, so a second child from him might be a ממזר. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees, but his words are unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught, the opening of a ברייתא
The High Priest, who needs the purest family line
A child born from a forbidden relationship such as with a brother's wife
Because of a doubt

steps.confusionAlert: The first child is kosher even if he turns out to be the dead husband's. The problem only starts with the second child, because then the יבום itself may have been forbidden.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The first child is fit to be a High Priest,
and the second is a ממזר because of a doubt.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
There is no ממזר from a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the case of the משנה and brings a ברייתא about the children's status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First child is fully kosher; second child is a ממזר because of a doubt; רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says there is no ממזר from a doubt.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is saying, since the disagreement is unclear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of the ברייתא. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not clear what 'a ממזר from a doubt' means, or what רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is denying. Both sides seem to agree the child might be a ממזר, so the real difference needs to be spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? A request to explain unclear words
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the ברייתא quoted in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagree about.

steps.title: אביי: the first view treats him as a doubt and forbids a ממזרת
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains: the תנא קמא says the second child is a doubtful ממזר, so he may not marry a ממזרת. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says he is treated as a definite ממזר, so he may marry a ממזרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what it means: the first child is fit to be a כהן גדול, and the second is a doubtful ממזר and may not marry a ממזרת. רבי אליעזר says: he is not a doubtful ממזר but a definite ממזר, and he may marry a ממזרת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first explanation of the ברייתא. The whole argument is about whether this child may marry a ממזרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doubtful ממזר is stuck both ways: he may not marry a regular Jewish woman, since he may be a ממזר, and he may not marry a ממזרת, since he may not be one. According to אביי, the תנא קמא holds that. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב treats him as a full ממזר, so at least a ממזרת is allowed for him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
Someone who may or may not be a ממזר
A female ממזר
Forbidden

phrases.english: Abaye said, this is what it means:
The first child is fit to be a High Priest,
and the second is a doubtful ממזר, and is forbidden to a ממזרת.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ סְפֵק מַמְזֵר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: he is not a doubtful ממזר,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from the ברייתא, just called by a shorter name.

phrases.english: but a definite ממזר, and is permitted to a ממזרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תנא קמא: doubtful ממזר, forbidden to a ממזרת. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: treated as definite ממזר, permitted to a ממזרת.

steps.title: רבא: the opposite reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא flips אביי's reading: the תנא קמא treats the second child as a definite ממזר because of the doubt, so he may marry a ממזרת. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says he is only a doubtful ממזר and may not marry a ממזרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, this is what it means: the first child is fit to be a כהן גדול, and the second is treated as a definite ממזר because of the doubt, and may marry a ממזרת. And רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: he is not a definite ממזר because of a doubt, but a doubtful ממזר, and may not marry a ממזרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second explanation that is the exact opposite of אביי's. The two positions stay the same, but they are given to the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אביי and רבא agree the argument is whether a doubtful ממזר may marry a ממזרת. They only disagree about who says what. For רבא, 'ממזר מספק' in the ברייתא means 'a full ממזר because of the doubt', and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב denies that.

keyTerms.meaning: Treated as a definite ממזר even though it comes from a doubt
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא say the argument is about a doubtful ממזר marrying a ממזרת. אביי: the תנא קמא forbids and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב permits. רבא: the reverse.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. The same two positions appear in both; אביי and רבא only switch which side holds which.

phrases.english: Rava said, this is what it means:
The first child is fit to be a High Priest,
and the second is a definite ממזר because of a doubt
and is permitted to a ממזרת.
And Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
There is no definite ממזר from a doubt.
Rather, he is a doubtful ממזר, and is forbidden to a ממזרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite explanation to אביי's in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תנא קמא: definite ממזר because of the doubt, permitted to a ממזרת. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: only a doubtful ממזר, forbidden to a ממזרת.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree about רבי אלעזר's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the root of the argument between אביי and רבא is רבי אלעזר's opinion in a משנה. רבי אלעזר allows definite with definite, but forbids any match that involves a doubtful person.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about רבי אלעזר's view, as the משנה teaches: רבי אלעזר says a definite person with a definite person is permitted. A definite with a doubtful, a doubtful with a definite, and a doubtful with a doubtful are all forbidden. These are the doubtful ones: a שתוקי, an אסופי, and a כותי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what is really behind the argument of אביי and רבא from the last two steps. It quotes a משנה where רבי אלעזר sets the rules for who may marry whom when someone's status is in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real argument is whether the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר, who forbids a doubtful person to marry a definite or doubtful one. Steps 21 and 22 show how this works. אביי does not rule like רבי אלעזר, so he reads רבי אליעזר בן יעקב as permitting the doubtful child to marry a ממזרת. רבא does rule like רבי אלעזר, so he reads רבי אליעזר בן יעקב as forbidding it.

keyTerms.meaning: they disagree about
people whose flawed status is certain, such as definite ממזרים
people whose flawed status is in doubt
a child whose mother is known but whose father is unknown
a foundling, a baby found abandoned with no known parents
a Samaritan, whose status is doubtful

steps.confusionAlert: Even two doubtful people may not marry each other. Each one might be a ממזר while the other is not, so the doubt goes both ways.

phrases.english: And they disagree about the view of רבי אלעזר.
phrases.notes: "They" are אביי and רבא from the last two steps.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: רבי אלעזר says:
Definite ones with definite ones are permitted,
definite ones with doubtful ones, and doubtful ones with definite ones,
and doubtful ones with doubtful ones, are forbidden.
And these are the doubtful ones:
A child of unknown father, a foundling, and a Samaritan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what lies underneath the argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the real point of argument between אביי and רבא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר, who forbids a doubtful person to marry a definite or doubtful one. Each reads רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to fit his view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the יבום case to the general marriage rules for people of doubtful status.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that רב ruled the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the הלכה is like רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a practical ruling. A doubtful person may not marry anyone of flawed status, whether definite or doubtful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבי אלעזר's opinion into practical הלכה. It also sets up the next step, where שמואל objects to this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the practical law follows

phrases.english: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
The הלכה is like רבי אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר: a doubtful person may not marry a definite or a doubtful person of flawed status.

steps.title: שמואל challenges with הלל's list of ten groups
steps.stepSummary: שמואל quotes a ברייתא from הלל listing ten family groups that came up from בבל and may all marry one another. That list includes doubtful people marrying definite ones, so it argues against ruling like רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: When I said this before שמואל, he told me: הלל taught that ten family groups came up from בבל: כהנים, לויים, ישראלים, חללים, converts, freed slaves, ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקים and אסופים. All of them may marry one another. And you say the הלכה is like רבי אלעזר?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה tells how שמואל reacted to רב's ruling. שמואל brings הלל's ברייתא to show that the ruling cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In הלל's list, doubtful groups (שתוקים, אסופים) are allowed to marry definite groups such as ממזרים. That is exactly the kind of match רבי אלעזר forbids. So שמואל asks how רב could rule like רבי אלעזר against הלל's ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: family groups, classes of lineage
children of a כהן's forbidden marriage, who lose כהונה status
freed slaves
descendants of the גבעונים, who may not marry into ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: any doubtful person is forbidden to marry anyone of flawed status. רב rules like him. שמואל objects with הלל's ברייתא, where doubtful and definite groups may marry each other.

phrases.english: When I said it before שמואל,
phrases.notes: "I" is רב יהודה, telling how שמואל reacted to רב's ruling.

phrases.english: he said to me: הלל taught:
Ten family groups came up from בבל:
כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים,
חללים, converts, freed slaves,
ממזרים, נתינים, children of unknown father, and foundlings.
And all of them are permitted to marry one another.
And you say the הלכה is like רבי אלעזר?!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אֲמַר לִי: הִלֵּל שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הלל's ברייתא allows doubtful groups to marry definite ממזרים. רבי אלעזר forbids exactly that, so ruling like him goes against הלל.

steps.title: אביי follows שמואל and reads רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to fit הלל
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds like שמואל, who rules like הלל. So he explains רבי אליעזר בן יעקב in a way that agrees with that הלכה, so the two הלכות do not clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי holds like שמואל, who said the הלכה follows הלל. So he explains רבי אליעזר בן יעקב in line with that הלכה, so that one הלכה does not contradict another הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי read the argument the way he did in step 16. He was trying to make רבי אליעזר בן יעקב fit the הלכה of הלל, which he accepts from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל (step 20) ruled like הלל's list, which lets doubtful people marry definite ones. It is also an accepted rule that we usually follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. If רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagreed with הלל, the two accepted rulings would clash, so אביי reads him in a way that matches הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (a certain opinion)
He sets it up, meaning he explains an opinion in a certain way
In line with the הלכה
So that ... not; in order to avoid
One הלכה would contradict another הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא are not arguing about what the words of the ברייתא mean on their own. Each one starts from a ruling he already accepts, and then reads רבי אליעזר בן יעקב so that it fits that ruling.

phrases.english: Abaye holds like Shmuel,
who said: the halacha follows Hillel,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹקֵי לַהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: and so he explains Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov
in line with the halacha,
so that there should not be a contradiction
of one halacha against another halacha.
phrases.notes: The two rulings are following הלל and the usual rule that we follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After שמואל's ruling like הלל in step 20, the גמרא shows that this ruling is what drives אביי's reading in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי's reading comes from accepting שמואל's ruling like הלל, and wanting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to agree with it.

steps.title: רבא follows רב and reads רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to fit רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds like רב, who rules like רבי אלעזר. So he explains רבי אליעזר בן יעקב in a way that agrees with that הלכה, to avoid a clash. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא holds like רב, who said the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר. So he explains רבי אליעזר בן יעקב in line with that הלכה, so that there should not be a contradiction...
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives the same explanation for רבא. He reads רבי אליעזר בן יעקב so that it fits רבי אלעזר, whom רב ruled like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב (step 19) ruled like רבי אלעזר, who forbids any marriage where one side is doubtful. רבא accepts that ruling, so he reads רבי אליעזר בן יעקב as saying the doubtful child may not marry a ממזרת (step 17). That way the ruling like רבי אלעזר and the rule of following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Like רב, following his ruling from step 19
The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר: doubtful people may not marry definite ones
The opinion of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument between אביי and רבא comes down to which ruling each one accepts. אביי follows שמואל, who rules like הלל. רבא follows רב, who rules like רבי אלעזר. Each reads רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to match.

phrases.english: Rava holds like Rav,
who said: the halacha follows Rabbi Elazar.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹקֵי לַהּ לִדְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: And so he explains the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov
in line with the halacha,
so that there should not be a contradiction

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This matches step 21: the same kind of explanation, now for רבא's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא's reading comes from accepting רב's ruling like רבי אלעזר, and wanting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to agree with it.
